test_policy.notes: Test-optional for first-year applicants with a high school GPA of 3.0 or higher and at least 16 college-preparatory courses; home-schooled, online high school and GED applicants must submit scores. The test-optional page does not address international applicants. If sent, Kean superscores SAT (highest ERW and Math) and uses the highest ACT composite. Test-optional admits still take placement tests and are not eligible for merit scholarships.

requirements.notes: International applicants submit a course-by-course transcript evaluation (including GPA) from a NACES-affiliated agency. Two English-language recommendation letters and a 1-2 page personal essay are recommended on the international page; the test-optional page lists a transcript, two letters, an essay and an activities list as required for test-optional applicants. A promo code waiving the $75 fee is available by attending a virtual information session.

deadlines.label: Preferred international freshman application deadline (fall 2027)
deadlines.notes: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis after this date. The FAQ prints no year, so fall 2027 is assumed.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Required if secondary education was in a non-English-primary country. A waiver can be requested with official documentation that secondary school instruction was in English; applicants to fully online programs are not eligible. Scores must be from the past two years and sent directly by the testing agency. Kean has no ESL program; the SUPERA Spanish-speaking program lets freshmen take general education courses in Spanish while completing ESL requirements and has no English test or SAT requirement.

english.notes: Exams taken after Jan 21, 2026: the page prints 'a minimum total score of 4' without naming the scale (presumably the new 1-6 scale); confirm with admissions.

aid.notes: No international scholarship names or amounts were found on Kean's international admissions pages. Starting fall 2026 the Board of Trustees eliminated out-of-state tuition, so international students pay the same rate as New Jersey residents (about $16,370 per year for tuition and fees in 2026-27). Test-optional admits cannot receive merit scholarships.

cost.notes: Cost of attendance 2026-27, full-time undergraduate living on campus (double occupancy): tuition and fees $16,370, housing and food $20,168, books $1,280, transportation $1,620, personal $1,916, loan fees $68, total $41,422. Tuition = 2 x $6,788.50 and fees = $2,793.67 (rounded) per the Student Accounting schedule. Out-of-state tuition no longer exists (Board vote of Sept 15, 2025, effective fall 2026), so international students pay this single rate

sat.note: CEEB code printed on the international freshmen page.

act.note: The international freshmen page gives only the CEEB code 2517 for SAT; no separate ACT code is printed.

toefl.note: No TOEFL institution code is printed on the pages reviewed; scores must be sent directly by the testing agency.
